title: Kubernetes egress rate limits for inference workloads — draft playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook sketches a low-risk, staged procedure to introduce egress rate limiting for inference-heavy Kubernetes workloads in private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Goal: bound request concurrency and external connection churn so customer NAT/egress gateways don't get overwhelmed during high token generation bursts, while keeping tail latency and token reliability acceptable for Redwood inference instances running in-customer clusters.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to k8s clusters used by Private deployments (Redwood Private).
- Clusters use Calico CNI + standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicy semantics. Some customers run Istio/Envoy as a sidecar egress gateway — we support both patterns.
- Inference services are stateful deployments (longer-lived pods) that maintain GRPC streams to model runtimes. We care about connection count, new-connection rate, and per-pod outbound request concurrency.

High-level strategy:
1) Introduce a lightweight Envoy sidecar-based egress-proxy for inference pods to enforce per-pod/concurrency shaping.
2) Provide Terraform module to deploy egress-proxy DaemonSet and ServiceAccount for each customer cluster.
3) Deploy Calico egress NetworkPolicy to prevent direct outbound to allowed external ranges (force through proxy).
4) Gradual rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of inference replicas. Canary metrics and automatic rollback threshold.

Key success metrics (canary):
- 99th percentile tail-token-latency delta <= +25% compared to baseline
- Error rate (generation 5xx / transport errors) increase <= 0.5% absolute
- NAT port exhaustion alerts: zero occurrences during canary windows

Terraform module notes (sketch):
- module "egress_proxy" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//egress-proxy"
    namespace = var.namespace
    proxy_image = var.egress_proxy_image // default: redwood/egress-proxy:2024.11
    concurrency_limit = var.concurrency_limit // default 64
    rate_limit_rps = var.rate_limit_rps // default 20
    force_iptables_redirect = var.force_iptables_redirect // bool
  }

Important implementation details:
- Proxy must be L7-aware for GRPC streaming. Use xDS config (Envoy) with HTTP/2/GRPC concurrency counters, not naive token bucket only.
- For environments without sidecars, provide a cluster-level egress-gateway DaemonSet + iptables TPROXY redirect; Terraform module should expose toggle.
- Calico policy to deny egress to 0.0.0.0/0 except to the egress-proxy service CIDR: this forces pods through proxy during rollout.

Calico NetworkPolicy example (draft):
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-pod-egress-to-proxy
spec:
  selector: has(label,"app") && app == "inference"
  egress:
  - action: Allow
    protocol: TCP
    destination:
      selector: "k8s-app == 'egress-proxy'"
  - action: Deny
  types: ["Egress"]

Rollout checklist (canary):
- Create feature branch for kustomize/helm changes that inject the sidecar (or annotate pods to use proxy).
- Deploy proxy DaemonSet with debug logging enabled in staging.
- Canary batch 1: select a single small inference service (non-critical) at 1% traffic with proxy annotation. Monitor 1h.
- Canary batch 2: ramp to 10% over 2 hours if metrics pass.
- Canary batch 3: 50% over 24 hours; run synthetic prompt floods at 2x expected load.
- Full rollout: remaining 50% + config drift check.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Add Prometheus exporters on proxy: envoy_connection_count, envoy_active_streams, envoy_upstream_5xx, envoy_retries.
- Grafana dashboard: per-cluster and per-service panels for active streams, new-conn/s, p99 token latency.
- Alert: env_upstream_5xx_rate > 0.5% for 10m -> rollback plan.

Rollback plan:
- Immediately unset pod annotation to bypass proxy (if annotation used).
- If forced by Calico policy, apply emergency patch to allow direct egress to model endpoints while rolling back proxy DaemonSet.
- Notify SRE/solutions-eng and open JIRA issue with logs/trace ids.

Testing and validation commands (examples):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -l app=inference -o wide
- kubectl exec -it pod/<inference-pod> -- ss -tnp | grep 443  # verify connections now go to envoy
- curl -sS http://proxy-metrics-service:9901/clusters | jq '.cluster_stats[] | {name, upstream_rq_5xx}'

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default concurrency_limit for small instances (gpt-small style) vs large (gpt-xl style). Proposal: 64 / pod for small; 256 for large — need perf validate.
- How to handle long-running KV-cache connections to model host? We need sticky upstream selection to avoid connection churn.
- Tradeoffs for using cluster-level gateway vs pod sidecars for latency-sensitive inference paths.
- Add terraform output that prints the required pod annotation with HMAC token for proxy to authenticate.

Appendix: quick HCL snippet to toggle iptables redirect (module variable mapping):
variable "force_iptables_redirect" {
  type = bool
  default = false
}

module "egress_proxy" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//egress-proxy"
  namespace = "redwood-inference"
  proxy_image = "ghcr.io/redwood/egress-proxy:2025-01-10"
  concurrency_limit = 128
  rate_limit_rps = 40
  force_iptables_redirect = true
}

Notes to self:
- Coordinate with solutions-eng before any on-prem rollout. Customers with strict egress filtering need pre-approved CIDR allowances for proxy health checks.
- Schedule a simulated NAT port exhaustion test in staging to validate behavior (we'll use a small test cluster with synthetic clients).

References / related PRs:
- github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/89  (egress-proxy module initial commit)
- JIRA-INFR-4567 (egress-hardening epic)
- CONFLUENCE-1234-egress-design

Contact: Jordan Kim (owner) — ping in #eng-private-deployments on slack for urgent changes.

End of draft.
